subject.title: Add external event hooks for quota and provider state changes

question: Should CodexBar accept persistent, opt-in user-configured external command hooks as a supported core feature and security boundary once exact argv round-tripping is fixed?
rationale: The patch is not merely internal wiring: it adds shared configuration, settings and CLI surfaces, and intentional local code execution whose long-term support and trust model require repository-owner intent.

options.title: Accept after argv repair
options.body: Sponsor the core hooks feature after the editor preserves exact argument arrays and the documented execution safeguards remain covered.

options.title: Decline or defer core hooks
options.body: Keep CodexBar observability-only for now and close or narrow the PR rather than committing to a persistent command-execution contract.

recommendation.title: Accept after argv repair
recommendation.body: Sponsor the core hooks feature after the editor preserves exact argument arrays and the documented execution safeguards remain covered.

likelyOwner.reason: As repository owner, this person is the clearest available authority for the new core configuration and command-execution contract.
